newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt - stake plan won't hurt rival airports.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt - stake plan won't hurt rival airports.

text.p: Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG), owner and manager of Frankfurt Airport, said on Monday it did not plan any shifts in air traffic as part of a possible acquisition of stakes in Cologne/Bonn or Hanover airports.
"A shift of traffic between the airports is not planned and dictatorial measures never work in any case," FAG management board chairman Wilhelm Bender said in a statement.
"But there certainly are possibilities for cooperation which would be useful to both sides.

The statement said FAG planned to hold talks with the aim of taking stakes in Cologne/Bonn or Hanover airports. It denied reports in local Cologne newspapers that FAG was planning a hostile takeover of Cologne airport.

FAG said its opportunities for expansion were at present limited to its site in Frankfurt and that its planned acquisition of share stakes would contribute towards securing and creating jobs in Germany.

FAG said it was already cooperating with airports in Germany and abroad for example Leipzig, Saarbruecken, Mallorca, Tenerife, Madrid and Athens to develop regional markets. All participants were benefiting from that cooperation, it said.
